article_title: Learning curve for transcatheter aortic valve replacement for native aortic regurgitation: Safety and technical performance study.
citation: Liu L , Zhang J , Peng Y , et al. (2020). Learning curve for transcatheter aortic valve replacement for native aortic regurgitation: Safety and technical performance study. Clinical Cardiology. 2020;43:475–482. https://doi.org/10.1002/clc.23332
title: J-Valve self-expanding transcatheter heart valve system for native aortic regurgitation
description: The J-Valve system (JieCheng Medical Technology Co., Ltd., Suzhou, China) is described as "a self‐expanding transcatheter heart valve with a unique two‐piece structure design that consists of three U‐shaped graspers encircling the valve stents." It was certified for AR and AS by the China Food and Drug Administration in 2017 and was the device used for all 134 transapical TAVR procedures in this single-center learning-curve study, deployed without rapid ventricular pacing with TEE guidance.
requirements: Performed in a fully equipped hybrid OR by an interdisciplinary team with a full cardiopulmonary bypass circuit on standby
constraints: In this study it was used only via the transapical approach by a single team at one center for native AR patients meeting specified annulus (19–29 mm) and aortic diameter (<50 mm) criteria
target_learners: High-risk patients aged ≥60 with moderate-severe or severe native aortic regurgitation
target_learning_goals: Treatment of native aortic regurgitation via transcatheter valve replacement
examples: All 134 study patients underwent transapical J-valve implantation through a 3–5 cm left intercostal incision with two-stage clasper positioning and deployment without rapid ventricular pacing
